title: Association between levels of persistent organic pollutants in adipose tissue and cryptorchidism in early childhood: a case-control study.
ehr_evidence: Obstetric data (maternal smoking, gestational diabetes, length of gestation, mother's weight before pregnancy, birth weight, parity) were obtained from medical records, while the primary exposure data came from subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsies analysed for PCBs, PCDD/Fs and PBDEs by gas chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry.
summary: A non-matched case-control study of 44 cryptorchid cases and 38 controls (boys operated at Turku University Hospital, Finland and Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, 2002-2006) examining associations between prenatal exposure to persistent organic pollutants (PCBs, PCDD/Fs, PBDEs) in adipose tissue and risk of congenital cryptorchidism.
key_findings: Adjusted total-TEq was positively associated with cryptorchidism [OR 3.21, 95% CI 1.29-9.09, p=0.02].
Adjusted sum of PCDD/Fs was positively associated with cryptorchidism [OR 3.69, 95% CI 1.45-10.9, p=0.01].
Adjusted sum of PCBs was close to significant [OR 1.92, 95% CI 0.98-4.01, p=0.07].
Sum of PBDEs was not associated with cryptorchidism [OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.47-1.54, p=0.61].
There were no associations between unadjusted chemical concentrations and the risk of cryptorchidism.

In sensitivity analysis restricted to term-born boys operated under 5 years whose mothers had no gestational diabetes, total-TEq (OR 3.47, 95% CI 1.15-12.9, p=0.04) and sum of PCDD/Fs (OR 10.2, 95% CI 2.36-65.5, p=0.005) remained positively associated.
Mothers of cryptorchid boys were significantly older (p=0.04) and had longer gestation (p=0.04) than controls.
captured_features: Adipose tissue concentrations of sum of PCBs, sum of PCDD/Fs, sum of PBDEs, and total-TEq
Duration of breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding
population: Boys operated for cryptorchidism (44 cases) and for inguinal, umbilical hernia or hydrocele (38 controls) at Turku University Hospital, Finland and Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark, 2002-2006; children under 5 years in Finland, mean age at operation 2.3-2.9 years.
exposure_domain: Persistent organic pollutants / endocrine disrupting chemicals (PCBs, PCDD/Fs, PBDEs)
limitations: Small sample size limiting statistical power.
Control group included boys with inguinal hernia, which has been associated with cryptorchidism.
Unable to adjust for lipid content of samples, increasing measurement error.
Danish obstetric and breastfeeding data collected ~10 years after operation, raising recall bias concerns.
No data on body size of children.
Recruited from pediatric surgery departments, limiting generalizability to mild, non-operated cryptorchidism.
